commit.subject: LU-20911 lfsck: check the layout of EC files
commit.message:
LU-20911 lfsck: check the layout of EC files

LFSCK only accepted the layout of an EC file, with its parity
components, when it rebuilt it from orphan OST objects.  Its scans
skipped EC files, and when an OST with lfsck_verify_pfid enabled asked
the MDT to verify an EC object whose parent FID or stripe index did
not match the RPC, the MDT refused it, so the OST kept returning
-EINPROGRESS and the client resent the I/O forever.

LFSCK checks layouts and the consistency of MDT and OST objects, not
file contents, and that works for the objects of parity components as
for those of data components, so accept EC layouts everywhere, and
drop the argument of lfsck_layout_verify_header() that selected them.

A repair that gives a component a new empty OST object, for a
dangling reference with "lfsck --create-ostobj" or for an object
shared with another file, would leave an EC component without its
parity or data.  A data component whose in-sync parity can rebuild
one more stripe of its raid set gets a dummy slot instead, as the
orphan handling leaves for a lost object, so that EC reads rebuild
that stripe from parity, as clients with
https://review.whamcloud.com/71263 ("LU-20911 lov: rebuild EC
stripes with no object from parity") do, and the object of the
other file is no longer referenced.  Otherwise it gets the empty
object as before.  A parity component still gets the new object,
but is marked stale first, with the file write pending, so that a
resync rewrites it, unless no data mirror would then be in sync.
If its data component already has a dummy slot, a resync could not
regenerate the parity, so its lost object also gets a dummy slot
while the remaining parity can still rebuild the data, and the
parity stays in use.  Since a parity object may hold parity of any
raid set, lost parity objects count against every raid set of the
data component.

When an OST with lfsck_verify_pfid enabled was asked to verify the
parent FID of an object that it was already verifying, it would leak
a reference on the object, and the OST would then hit an LBUG at
unmount.  Take the reference only when the object is queued.

Add sanity-lfsck test_55 to read and resync an EC file whose data and
parity objects name a parent that does not exist, with
lfsck_verify_pfid enabled, test_56 to repair an EC file whose data
and parity objects are all lost, test_58 to repair a 2+2 file that
lost one data and one parity object, and test_59 to repair an EC data
object shared with another file.

Test-Parameters: trivial testlist=sanity-lfsck
Fixes: 730a204e7366 ("LU-3951 lfsck: OST-object inconsistency self detect/repair")
